summary: A 500 body should be a stable generic message plus a request id the client can quote; it must never include stack traces, secrets, or PII. The request id is the join key to logs.
evidence: GET /debug/error ASGI: DEBUG_ERROR_STATUS 500 DEBUG_ERROR_BODY {"detail":"internal server error"} DEBUG_ERROR_X_REQUEST_ID req-624f08cc HAS_TRACEBACK_IN_BODY False
Same request logs ERROR unhandled exception request_id=req-624f08cc stack_trace=Traceback ... RuntimeError: forced observability test error. Engineers get the stack; the client does not.

Customer report join key: X-Request-ID header (also logged as request_id). Without it you cannot grep one request out of unstructured 2am noise. Never put JWT_SECRET, DATABASE_URL, or the exception message that might contain a connection string in the JSON body.
